# Understanding Cairns: Complete Summary

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn grow. The new height equals: current height + stride + (how many complete strides fit into the current height). The key is that you count strides based on the height *before* the pulse happens, not after.

## Repeated Pulses
When a cairn pulses multiple times, you must apply each pulse individually. After each pulse, the height changes, so the stride count changes too. You can't use a shortcut—you have to recalculate from scratch each time.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a single pulse. You calculate marks lost by dividing the new pulsed height by the leak size and taking the whole number part. The leak applies to the height *after* the pulse, not before. Then you subtract the lost marks.

## Cycles with Drains
A cycle consists of one pulse followed by a fixed drain amount. Unlike leaks (which are proportional), drains remove the same number of marks every cycle. You repeat cycles until the height reaches zero or below, applying pulse then drain each time.

## Merging Cairns
When combining two cairns, use the formula: floor(w × q1) + floor((1 − w) × q2) + b, where w is the share (in tenths), q1 and q2 are the heights, and b is the tether. The shares must add to 1. Each component matters.

## Working Backwards (Origins)
To find a starting height given a final height and pulses, test candidate answers by applying the pulses forward and see which produces the target.
